answer: The protocol mandates 1,000 unique location proofs to authenticate each agent by measuring signal transit via a fixed relay grid. An issuer assigns distinct spatial coordinates; each signed receipt proves the agent occupied that site as the dawn breaks. A verifier reproduces failure by re-running logs, mapping the signal kernel to detect latency fraud. A sonnet of checks ensures no two identities overlap. An honest participant incurs linear travel costs, while an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes faces extreme spatial congestion that renders spoofing non-viable.
